newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia launches 7 satellites for Iridium network.
newsitem.headline: Russia launches 7 satellites for Iridium network.

text.p: Russia launched seven U.S.-made telecommunication satellites for the Iridium LLC consortium's global space communications network Wednesday, a military forces spokesman said.
He said a heavy Russian-made Proton booster blasted off from the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
"The satellites, which weighed 650 kg (1,430 pounds) each, should reach the 518 km (321 miles) orbit in about two hours," the spokesman said.
The booster is owned by Moscow-based rocket maker Khrunichev, which will make two additional launches in September and early next year, each carrying a seven Iridium satellites into orbit.
A Khrunichev spokesman said last week that three launches, involving 21 satellites, would cost $179 million in total.
Last month Iridium began a project to place 66 satellites in low earth orbit when it sent five probes into space aboard a U.S. Delta rocket.
Khrunichev has invested $80 million of its own funds in the project, which will provide former Soviet republics with cellular phone service.
Iridium LLC is a consortium including Iridium World Communications Ltd, Motorola Inc., Sprint Corp., Lockheed Martin Corp. and Raytheon Co.
